rows.description: Battery Electric Car example, rebuilt on the 2021 Cupra Born 58 kWh (CON-03): topology, six cases (City Cycle on the default profile DR-06; WLTC class 3b, the same with the heating/air-con load at 2.5 kW, and the same at -7 degC and at 35 degC (CON-30, the Ambient presets' temperatures), all on the bundled cycle DR-25; and a live 10x City Cycle), an Ambient at its defaults (20 degC, 101.325 kPa, the air the model had without one) and its values. From FASTSim's 2021_Cupra_Born.csv: mass 1,927 kg, Cd 0.27, frontal area 2.31 m2, wheel radius 0.3488 m, wheel inertia 0.815 kg m2, rolling resistance 0.011, 61 % of the weight on the driven axle (30.5 % per driven wheel, 19.5 % per other wheel; the wheels tagged Front (FL, FR) and Rear (RL, RR) by their labels, CG height 0 so the loads do not shift), battery 62 kWh with a 4 % floor (58 kWh usable), auxiliary load 0.25 kW, transmission efficiency 98 % (final drive 98 %, differential 100 %), recuperation weight 98 % (maxRegen), motor 150 kW. Not from FASTSim: motor maps (DR-22 to DR-24) and final drive 12.8. Every other value is a component default (DR-04 to DR-17).
rows.source: FASTSim 2.1.5 (NREL, now National Laboratory of the Rockies; https://github.com/NatLabRockies/fastsim), fastsim/resources/vehdb/2021_Cupra_Born.csv, which cites automobile-catalog.com and carexpert.com.au for its values; final drive chosen for LightSim (see notes); topology and City Cycle cases from the earlier example (provenance unknown)

rows.description: P2 Hybrid Car example, rebuilt as a Hyundai Ioniq Hybrid Blue class car (CON-02): topology plus a 0.5 kW '12 V Loads' consumer, the Hybrid Control Unit script (a charge-sustaining strategy with a copy of the engine curve DR-27 and the motor's 170 N m / 32 kW), four cases (EPA UDDS and EPA HWFET on the bundled cycles DR-34 and DR-35, the Mixed Cycle DR-03 and its live copy) with charge-balanced start SOCs of 56.34 / 58.92 / 51.96 %. From the EPA 2022 Test Car List (Ioniq, test MHYX10066415): test mass 1,474 kg (ETW 3,250 lb); road load A 15.431 lbf, B 0.32897 lbf/mph, C 0.014602 lbf/mph2 (target coefficients), entered as 68.64 N, 0.9093 N/(km/h) and 0.025078 N/(km/h)2 with 'Coefficients Include Driveline Losses' on (since MOD-11, 0.3; before, fitted over UDDS and HWFET as rolling resistance 0.0064 and Cd x A 0.70 m2, Cd 0.318 with the default 2.2 m2, which the example keeps for the drag-and-rolling-resistance mode); N/V 32.6 1/min per mph gives the final drive 3.38 with the default 6th gear (0.7) and a 0.31 m wheel. Wheels: 30 % of the weight on each front wheel and 20 % on each rear one, tagged Front (FL, FR) and Rear (RL, RR) by their labels, CG height 0 so the loads do not shift. From FASTSim: 0.5 kW auxiliary load and 95 % transmission efficiency (final drive 98 %, differential 100 %, gearbox default 97 %) as in its HEV files, wheel inertia 0.815 kg m2 (its default). Background knowledge (unverified): engine 77 kW / 147 N m, motor 32 kW / 170 N m, battery 1.56 kWh at 240 V, 195/65 R15 tyres (0.31 m). Synthetic: engine, motor and battery maps (DR-27 to DR-33), battery resistance 0.1 ohm, the control strategy. Every other value is a component default (DR-04 to DR-17).
rows.source: EPA 2022 Test Car List (22-tstcar.csv, as shipped in FASTSim 2.1.5 (NREL, now National Laboratory of the Rockies; https://github.com/NatLabRockies/fastsim) resources/epa_vehdb); FASTSim 2.1.5 resources/FASTSim_py_veh_db.csv and parameters.py; Hyundai's published figures (background knowledge, unverified); Synthetic / created for LightSim in the CON-02/CON-03 example rebuild; topology from the earlier example (provenance unknown)

Maps, curves and profiles have their own rows (DR-05 to DR-17). Not a default: the battery's 'Formula Student Electric' preset, output power limit 80 kW, power check window 0.5 s, voltage class 600 V.

rows.description: Formula Student electric car example 'FS Electric (generic)' (CON-33): a typical car, not a real one. Topology: one rear E-Motor, a 4.4 chain drive (97 %) and an open differential (98 %) to the rear wheels; the front wheels on their brakes only; no auxiliary load (FS low voltage runs from its own battery). Three cases: 'Acceleration 75 m' (kind acceleration, 75 m from a start line 0.3 m ahead, 25 s, 0.01 s step, reference time 3.91 s); 'Autocross (flying lap)' (lap mode on the Autocross layout of DR-38, 2 laps); 'Endurance energy' (lap mode, 23 laps = 22 km / 979 m rounded up, Store every 5, the Accumulator's Output Power Limit set to 30 kW by the case). Values: mass 280 kg with driver, Cd 1.2 x 1.0 m2, CG height 0.28 m, wheelbase 1.53 m, track widths 1.22 / 1.18 m, downforce area CzA 3.0 m2 with 45 % on the front axle; wheels 0.228 m radius (an 18 x 7.5-10 tyre), 0.2 kg m2, load shares 22.5 % front and 27.5 % rear each, mu 1.5, lateral mu 1.5, load sensitivity -0.2 per kN about a 700 N nominal load, friction ellipse exponent 2, slip stiffness 20, rolling resistance 0.015; brakes 500 N m front and 300 N m rear, 0.01 kg m2 each; Driver recuperation weight 100 %; E-Motor maps DR-42 to DR-44, maximum speed 6,500 1/min, rotor 0.02 kg m2, generator torque scale 40 % (full generator torque locks the rear wheels under braking once the load shifts forward); final drive inertias 0.002 / 0.005 kg m2, differential 0.005 kg m2; Accumulator 138s4p of 3.5 Ah cells: 14 Ah, OCV DR-45 (414-579.6 V), 7.21 kWh, 0.3 ohm, 30 kW charge, 100 % at the start, 5 % minimum, and the battery's Formula Student Electric preset (80 kW, 0.5 s window, 600 V class, held). Its description (the Open menu's entry) gives the rule values, the results to expect and the reference results below.
rows.source: Synthetic / created for LightSim in the CON-33 change: typical values, marked 'typical — replace with your data' in the example. Rule values are facts from Formula Student Rules 2026 v1.1 (FSG, https://www.formulastudent.de): T 2.9.1 wheelbase at least 1,525 mm, EV 2.2.1 80 kW at the accumulator outlet, EV 2.2.2 500 A, EV 4.1.1 600 V DC, D 5.1.1 75 m, D 5.2.3 staged 0.3 m behind the start line, D 7.1.3 about 22 km of endurance, D 9.2.1 the 25 s limit (driverless runs only), D 10.4.1 a 500 ms moving average. Reference results are facts from the FS Czech Republic 2025 EV results (https://www.fsczech.cz, read 2026-09-25): acceleration, the best times of 35 teams 3.51-6.44 s, median 3.91 s; efficiency, the consumption of the 14 scored teams 3.19-6.15 kWh, median 5.25 kWh.

rows.description: Efficient Electric Sedan example (CON-07), a 2022 Tesla Model 3 RWD class car on the Battery Electric Car's layout (DR-01): EPA city, highway and WLTC class 3b cases. From the EPA 2022 Test Car List (Model 3 RWD, test NTSL10071574): equivalent test weight 4,250 lb (1,928 kg), target road load A 37.17 lbf, B 0.0470 lbf/mph, C 0.0144 lbf/mph2 (entered as 165.33 N, 0.1299 N/(km/h), 0.024725 N/(km/h)2 with 'Coefficients Include Driveline Losses' on), rated 257 hp (192 kW), N/V 115.0 1/min per mph (reduction 9.0 with a 0.334 m wheel). From FASTSim 2.1.5's 2022_Tesla_Model_3_RWD.csv, values whose comment gives no source: battery 54 kWh, minimum SOC 5 %, 59 % of the weight on the driven axle; Cd 0.23 and 2.22 m2 (from arXiv:1908.08920, kept for comparison, not used with coefficients). Not taken: the file's mass and motor power, which it cites from evspecifications.com (a banned source, DATA-REGISTER.md rule 3). Tyre radius 0.334 m (235/45 R18, background knowledge, unverified). Motor maps: DR-98 to DR-100. Every other value is the Battery Electric Car's or a component default.
